bullets.note: Government forces are rushing to defend the city, sources told AFP

bullets.text: Iran's IRGC navy says an oil tanker struck naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire
bullets.note: Adds to tensions around a key oil shipping route

bullets.text: US air travel disruptions continue into a third day after Friday's ground stop
bullets.note: Airlines are still rebuilding schedules

bullets.text: Duffy says the air traffic control routers' ability to broadcast data has been turned off during the investigation
bullets.note: The router issue prompted Friday's nationwide ground stop

bullets.text: Jensen Huang is discussing a comeback as Nvidia CEO with allies, the FT reports
bullets.note: The fight over Nvidia's leadership continues

bullets.text: Bessent calls on Nvidia to explain whether it knowingly let its most advanced AI chips reach China
bullets.note: He said this matters more than the affair at the center of the scandal

bullets.text: Estonia is closing its border crossings with Russia after an alleged arson attempt at a drone factory
bullets.note: Tallinn says Russian military intelligence ordered it; eight people were arrested

bullets.text: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow immediate humanitarian access throughout Gaza
bullets.note: A joint statement on the dire situation in the enclave

bullets.text: Prince Harry makes his fourth surprise visit to Ukraine since 2022, meeting wounded veterans and medics
bullets.note: A high-profile show of support for Ukraine

bullets.text: Pope Leo demands justice for slain Indigenous leaders during his visit to Peru
bullets.note: The final full day of his South America tour

bullets.text: Cape Verde's President Jose Maria Neves easily wins re-election, provisional results show
bullets.note: Results from the archipelago's electoral commission

bullets.text: A cat feared lost in the deadly Brooklyn building collapse has been found safe
bullets.note: A bit of good news after the collapse that killed eight

bullets.text: England beats Spain 3-2 to end the world champions' 44-match unbeaten run in competitive games
bullets.note: Belgium also beat Italy 4-1 to reach the Nations League quarterfinals

recaps.title: Culture & entertainment
recaps.intro: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer won a softer-than-expected box office weekend, Phil Collins told the Rock Hall he is doing better, and SNL's Jensen Huang cold open kept the scandal in pop culture.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer opens at No. 1 with 19 million dollars, while How to Rob a Bank stumbles with 5 million
bullets.note: Depp's first studio film in eight years

bullets.text: Ebenezer reaches 42 million worldwide, as Ramayana nears 150 million and Godzilla Minus Zero passes 100 million
bullets.note: The global box office picture

bullets.text: Godzilla Minus Zero slides to No. 3 with 8.31 million, a 75 percent drop from its opening
bullets.note: Last weekend's leader fell fast

bullets.text: Domestic ticket sales are up 20 percent from last year as Hollywood awaits a Hunger Games prequel, Dune 3 and Avengers
bullets.note: A strong year for theaters heading into the holidays

bullets.text: Phil Collins tells the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame he is now a well man at his induction
bullets.note: He also said he hopes to perform and make new music again

bullets.text: Bowen Yang returns to SNL as Jensen Huang in a cold open about tech billionaires and honey pot plots
bullets.note: SNL took on the Nvidia scandal

bullets.text: Phoebe Bridgers performs with a black-light skeleton effect on SNL
bullets.note: One of the most talked-about musical moments of the night

bullets.text: SNL sets its December return with Amanda Seyfried as host and Don Toliver as musical guest
bullets.note: Seyfried's debut as host

bullets.text: Slow Horses will end with Season 8, Olivia Cooke says
bullets.note: The spy series is wrapping up

bullets.text: Kevin Feige says including the original X-Men in Avengers: Doomsday just felt right
bullets.note: The film opens next month

bullets.text: God of War Ragnarok is the top-grossing PlayStation Studios game of the PS5 era, at an estimated 1.4 billion dollars
bullets.note: It passes Spider-Man 2's 1.3 billion

recaps.title: Science & space
recaps.intro: ULA's Vulcan failed on its return to flight with 40 Amazon Leo satellites aboard, a day after Starship's first catch, while new brain, galaxy and allergy research filled out the day.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: ULA confirms Vulcan suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit
bullets.note: A failed return to flight for ULA's heavy rocket

bullets.text: Multiple sources say the Vulcan anomaly occurred in the booster stage, not the Centaur V upper stage or solid boosters
bullets.note: The cause is still unknown

bullets.text: Starship's Ship 42 rolls back to the Starbase production site after Flight 15
bullets.note: The first Ship to be caught has come home

bullets.text: Researchers publish the most detailed atlas of the basal ganglia, covering 25.5 million brain cells
bullets.note: A detailed map of a key brain region

bullets.text: New Euclid telescope images show close-ups of distant galaxies where stars are forming
bullets.note: The latest data release from the space telescope

bullets.text: Emerging evidence suggests the allergy drug omalizumab may reduce severe reactions for alpha-gal syndrome
bullets.note: A red meat allergy triggered by a tick bite

bullets.text: Doctors worry about rising measles cases among pregnant women as the outbreak grows
bullets.note: A risk to both mother and baby

bullets.text: A study finds cold therapy like ice baths may slow recovery after exercise rather than speed it
bullets.note: Challenges a popular recovery habit

bullets.text: Diet clues from a man who lived about 6,000 years ago hint he lived through a revolutionary change in human history
bullets.note: A window into prehistoric life

recaps.title: Pictures of the day
recaps.intro: Pope Leo among Andean families in Cusco, monster surf drawing crowds in Santa Cruz, Starship back in the tower's arms and a polar bear on the ice.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Pope Leo XIV greeted by people in colorful traditional Andean dress in Cusco, Peru
bullets.note: The final full day of his South America tour, at high altitude

bullets.text: Huge waves crash against the Santa Cruz shoreline as crowds gather to watch
bullets.note: Waves over 30 feet despite warnings to stay away

bullets.text: Starship's Ship 42 held in the tower's mechanical arms after Flight 15
bullets.note: The first Ship catch in the Starship program

bullets.text: A polar bear stands on sea ice beside open blue water
bullets.note: A striking wildlife portrait

bullets.text: Prince Harry shakes hands with a wounded veteran during a surprise visit to Ukraine
bullets.note: His fourth visit to the country since 2022

recaps.title: Week ahead
recaps.intro: Grammy nominations kick off the week, Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's IPO test the AI trade, and summits in Asia and a royal trip to India fill the calendar.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Grammy nominations are announced Monday at 7:45 a.m. ET, streaming live
bullets.note: The first look at the next Grammy Awards

bullets.text: The AI trade faces big tests this week, starting with Nvidia earnings and capped by Anthropic's IPO
bullets.note: Two of the biggest market events of the fall

bullets.text: Trump will take part in a first-ever U.S.-China-Russia leaders meeting at the APEC summit in China, U.S. officials say
bullets.note: A rare three-way meeting of the leaders

bullets.text: World leaders converge on the Philippines this week for a regional summit, many seeking deeper trade links
bullets.note: A hedge against rising US protectionism

bullets.text: Prince William and Kate travel to India this week, their first joint overseas trip since Kate's cancer diagnosis
bullets.note: A major royal tour

bullets.text: UK PM Burnham will say Monday that Brexit has not worked, ahead of a summit with the EU later this week
bullets.note: A push to seek a new deal with Europe

bullets.text: Duffy expects flights to return to full capacity Monday
bullets.note: After days of disruption from the ground stop

bullets.text: This week's AP Top 25 college football poll will not be released until Monday at 2 p.m. ET
bullets.note: One game changed the poll's schedule

bullets.text: Vermont turns warmer and sunnier after Monday, especially from Wednesday on
bullets.note: A break from the cool, cloudy weather

recaps.title: Politics & Washington
recaps.intro: Sunday's Washington talk centered on the ground stop, with Trump breaking his silence to blame the Biden administration and ask for money, while the Nvidia spy scandal widened toward Lutnick. Van Hollen pressed his challenge to Schumer.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Trump breaks his silence on the nationwide ground stop, blaming the Biden administration and calling on Congress for more money
bullets.note: The money would go to upgrade America's air traffic control system, the Post reports.

bullets.text: Duffy says the US has to get off old network, old telecom after an outage officials say stemmed from overloaded routers
bullets.note: The outage prompted the FAA to order a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.

bullets.text: Duffy pins the ground stop on Congress's lack of funding
bullets.note: Politico reports Duffy expects flights to return to full capacity Monday.

bullets.text: Van Hollen disputes Schumer's claim that he has the votes to stay Senate Democratic leader
bullets.note: Van Hollen told Fox he has the support of about 15 senators and growing ahead of the Dec. 1 leadership vote.

bullets.text: Van Hollen says he would not push right out of the gate to eliminate the filibuster
bullets.note: He told Fox it is a really important decision he would not make without consulting colleagues.

bullets.text: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agrees to testify behind closed doors on his relationship with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang
bullets.note: Rep. John Moolenaar announced it; Bloomberg says at least four congressional committees have called Huang to testify.

bullets.text: Bessent says Nvidia must go outside the company to find a new CEO
bullets.note: Politico reports Bessent also pushed back on the need for tighter chip sale legislation.

bullets.text: Sen. Blumenthal says Commerce Secretary Lutnick must go following the Nvidia scandal
bullets.note: Bessent and Congress are zeroing in on Lutnick's role in the Nvidia-Megaspeed scandal, The Hill reports.

bullets.text: Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the center of the Nvidia scandal, says suspected spy Alice Huang left in 2025
bullets.note: The company denied any wrongdoing, saying it conducts legitimate and lawful business.

bullets.text: Democrats now hold every House district touching Mexico and all four border-state governorships
bullets.note: Axios says the sweep gives Democrats new leverage over border spending and legal challenges in Trump's final two years.

bullets.text: Sen. Mark Kelly says an immigration deal with Trump would be a very positive thing
bullets.note: He called the border under Biden chaos but said the current administration is tearing communities apart.

bullets.text: The Justice Department sues Lyft, accusing it of discriminating against passengers with disabilities
bullets.note: A federal civil rights case against a major rideshare app.

recaps.title: World
recaps.intro: Iran's drone attack on a US radar site in Bahrain kept Gulf tensions high, while Southeast Asian leaders gathered for an ASEAN summit Trump is expected to join. Gaza buried 70 people recovered from rubble.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Iran's IRGC says it launched six drones at a US radar installation at an air base in Bahrain
bullets.note: Iran called it retaliation for a US strike on a telecom tower in Sirik; Arab states condemned the attack.

bullets.text: Iran rejects Germany's demand that it halt uranium enrichment
bullets.note: Its foreign ministry spokesperson said the right to enrichment is not something Germany, France or others granted.

bullets.text: A severe fuel crisis erupts in besieged Taiz as Yemen's Houthis battle government forces
bullets.note: Reuters reports anti-Houthi forces are retreating in Yemen.

bullets.text: Zelenskyy says speed restrictions on Starlink's military-grade internet service aided a wave of deadly Russian attacks
bullets.note: Starlink is a key communications link for Ukraine's forces.

bullets.text: Three ships are struck by drones in the Black Sea near a Romanian shipping canal, Romania's PM says
bullets.note: Drone strikes on shipping near a NATO member's coast.

bullets.text: ASEAN and China fail to conclude a South China Sea code of conduct
bullets.note: Southeast Asian leaders are meeting in the Philippines, and Trump is expected on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reports.

bullets.text: Protesters clash with police as they march toward the ASEAN summit venue in Manila
bullets.note: Hundreds were denouncing conflict in the Middle East and Trump's expected visit.

bullets.text: Gaza holds a mass funeral for 70 Palestinians whose bodies were recovered from under rubble
bullets.note: Al Jazeera says at least 8,000 more are believed to remain trapped.

bullets.text: Tens of thousands of Czechs rally against the government's plan for public media funding
bullets.note: The BBC says the plan would switch how public media is funded.

bullets.text: Almost 1,500 migrants arrive in Spain's Canary Islands, the most in a single day since 2020
bullets.note: The figure was reported by the EFE news agency.

bullets.text: Six months after Congo declared an Ebola outbreak, the disease remains out of control
bullets.note: Efforts to contain it are faltering, ABC reports.

bullets.text: Cape Verde votes in a presidential election featuring the country's first female presidential candidate
bullets.note: President Jose Maria Neves faces Joana Rosa.

recaps.title: Morning briefing
recaps.intro: Overnight brought a UPS and Copa jet collision in Miami, new Iranian strikes on Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, and more flight cancellations as airlines recover from Friday's ground stop. Starship's first tower catch led the good news.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet collide on a taxiway at Miami International Airport
bullets.note: Airport officials and the FAA confirmed the Saturday night collision.

bullets.text: Iran targets an air base in Bahrain, its first direct strike on the Gulf state in weeks
bullets.note: Bahrain says it intercepted the attack; Iran said a path to ending the conflict with the US remains open, Bloomberg reports.

bullets.text: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles headed toward Riyadh and drones in the Eastern Province
bullets.note: Gulf states faced missile and drone fire overnight, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Airlines cancel hundreds more departures Sunday as they rebuild schedules after the FAA ground stop
bullets.note: ABC News counted more than 900 Sunday cancellations on FlightAware overnight, with the number expected to rise.

bullets.text: SpaceX catches a returning Starship with the tower's mechanical arms for the first time
bullets.note: The ship was caught where its 22-hour journey began.

bullets.text: Judge blocks the Trump administration from closing East Potomac Golf Links in Washington
bullets.note: The judge ruled the administration probably violated federal environmental and administrative law.

bullets.text: NTSB recovers the data recorder from the tanker in the New Orleans cruise ship collision
bullets.note: It should help investigators reconstruct the Mississippi River crash.

bullets.text: Police lift an evacuation order after a bomb is found near an ethanol plant in central Illinois
bullets.note: Police had urged people within a mile of the plant to evacuate after a bomb threat.

bullets.text: Four grizzly bears captured in western Canada were behind the deaths of a mother and her adult daughter
bullets.note: Investigators believe it was a rare predatory attack.

bullets.text: US diesel falls below 6 dollars a gallon, a two-month low
bullets.note: Reuters cites easing tensions and weaker demand.

bullets.text: Yemen government forces withdraw from an area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control
bullets.note: The strait is a key shipping chokepoint.

bullets.text: Guatemala declares a state of emergency in two departments after a lawmaker is killed
bullets.note: The emergency decree follows the deadly attack.

bullets.text: Jordan sentences three men to death over a deadly church attack
bullets.note: The case stems from a deadly attack on a church, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Labour MPs try to block drilling at the Rosebank oil field in a first big rebellion against UK PM Andy Burnham
bullets.note: Bloomberg cites the Sunday Times.

recaps.title: AI & tech
recaps.intro: Nvidia's leadership fight kept going, with big investors and a petition seeking Jensen Huang's return while Washington moved on chip loopholes. Anthropic's IPO valuation and AI infrastructure deals filled out the day.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Two major investors urge Nvidia's board to consider the potential return of Jensen Huang
bullets.note: Altimeter and Atreides, which own 2.13 billion dollars in Nvidia, signed the letter, per CNBC via Techmeme.

bullets.text: A petition to reinstate Huang as Nvidia CEO tops 100,000 signatures, including Elon Musk
bullets.note: Organizers say more than 5,000 Nvidia staff signed, Business Insider reports.

bullets.text: Megaspeed says the businesswoman at the center of the Nvidia scandal left the company in August 2025
bullets.note: The chip firm is under scrutiny over export controls.

bullets.text: Commerce prepares to close a loophole giving Chinese AI firms access to restricted Nvidia chips through overseas data centers
bullets.note: The Information cites people familiar with the process.

bullets.text: Southeast Asian data centers gave Chinese companies computing power and cover for alleged chip smuggling
bullets.note: The WSJ investigation adds to pressure on chip export policy.

bullets.text: DeepSeek's 92 billion dollar valuation round drew Tencent and CATL
bullets.note: Backers also included companies pitched as a major source of black-market Nvidia chips, The Information says.

bullets.text: Anthropic prepares to go public at a valuation of up to 1.4 trillion dollars
bullets.note: One analyst puts its value at 1.7 trillion dollars ahead of the IPO.

bullets.text: Italy fines Meta 887 million dollars over Android users' data access
bullets.note: Reuters reports the fine centers on how Meta accessed Android users' data.

bullets.text: Firmus plans a 3 billion dollar fundraising that includes prepayments from Nvidia and Meta
bullets.note: The Australian Financial Review reported the plan, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Applied Digital has asked tenants like Oracle and Meta for billions in guarantees to secure power
bullets.note: Bloomberg reports the requests came before leases were finalized.

bullets.text: Google explores buying AI ad-creation tools as advertisers press for better AI ad features
bullets.note: Google is also paying Hightouch to move advertisers onto its customer data tools.

bullets.text: AI Futures Project now expects superhuman AI researchers by late 2027
bullets.note: That is earlier than its original forecast of 2029 or later.

bullets.text: Indian stocks roar back as the AI trade retreats
bullets.note: Global investors are returning to the 5.4 trillion dollar market, Bloomberg says.

bullets.text: Top scorer on a South Korean tax accountant exam confesses to cheating with generative AI
bullets.note: He turned himself in to police, Bloomberg reports.

recaps.title: Sports
recaps.intro: Giannis carried the Heat to a fourth straight win and Cooper Flagg passed Kobe on a record list. The Patriots play the Lions in Munich this morning, and Arch Manning rallied Texas past LSU.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Giannis Antetokounmpo posts 34 points, 14 rebounds and 8 assists as the Heat win a fourth straight
bullets.note: Klay Thompson added 26 against Detroit, outlasting 33 from Cade Cunningham.

bullets.text: Cooper Flagg passes Kobe Bryant for the second-most points by a teenager in NBA history
bullets.note: Flagg has 1,762 points; LeBron James holds the top spot with 2,362.

bullets.text: Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray become the first teammates tracked with 1,000-plus assists to each other
bullets.note: Tracking began in 1997-98; Denver won on the road.

bullets.text: Tyrese Proctor records his first career triple-double as a short-handed Cavaliers team beats Dallas
bullets.note: Cleveland had no available player averaging 25-plus minutes coming in.

bullets.text: Patriots WR A.J. Brown and RB Rhamondre Stevenson are expected to play against the Lions in Munich
bullets.note: Kickoff is 9:30 a.m. ET on Fox, per Mike Reiss.

bullets.text: Patriots place RB TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve with an illness
bullets.note: Stevenson is set to be active after no running back was elevated from the practice squad.

bullets.text: Chiefs DT Chris Jones has rejoined the team and is expected to play Sunday at Atlanta
bullets.note: Kansas City announced his return.

bullets.text: Saints activate RB Travis Etienne from injured reserve
bullets.note: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the move.

bullets.text: Jamie Benn reaches 1,000 career points in a Stars win
bullets.note: The Dallas bench emptied to celebrate the milestone.

bullets.text: Simon Holmstrom scores his first career hat trick
bullets.note: Matthew Schaefer had three assists in one period as the Islanders rolled.

bullets.text: Connor Hellebuyck stays undefeated for the Devils
bullets.note: New Jersey won again Saturday.

bullets.text: Svitolina and Andreeva meet in the WTA Finals championship
bullets.note: If Andreeva wins she goes undefeated and earns 3.37 million dollars.

bullets.text: Errani and Paolini reach the WTA Finals doubles final
bullets.note: They beat Guo and Mladenovic.

bullets.text: Arch Manning leads No. 6 Texas on a fourth-quarter comeback win at No. 21 LSU
bullets.note: It is Texas's fifth win over a ranked team this season, ESPN says.

bullets.text: Brian Kelly spoke with Maryland this week about its head coaching job
bullets.note: Maryland fired Mike Locksley on Oct. 21.

recaps.title: Vermont on X
recaps.intro: A quieter, cool Sunday follows a record-late first snow depth on Mount Mansfield. Deer season rule changes and winter shelter beds round out the local news.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Showers are less widespread today, but cloudy, cool weather continues with lingering mountain snow showers
bullets.note: A quieter Sunday after Saturday's rain and snow.

bullets.text: Mount Mansfield's snow stake records its first measurable snow depth, the latest such date on record
bullets.note: The previous latest dates were Nov. 9 in 1985 and 1956.

bullets.text: Hunters prepare for a major rule change in Vermont's deer rifle season on antlerless deer
bullets.note: Some seasoned hunters are wary of the change, VTDigger reports.

bullets.text: Clinton County warming center is moving to a new site with more beds ahead of winter
bullets.note: It adds shelter capacity across the lake as cold sets in.

bullets.text: Why only two health insurers sell plans on Vermont's exchange: the state is too small
bullets.note: Health insurance is a game of large numbers, and Vermont doesn't have them, VTDigger says.
